strengths: The hook copy is quick and funny (122-140 wpm): 'Spin a globe, and Earth looks like it's melting' and 'left the planet on the dashboard in July'. The 3D character watching a red drop slide off the globe (0:17-0:18) and the coin flip on 'just a coincidence?' (0:28-0:29) land. There's a flash-forward of the final Gondwana reveal at 0:31, as the playbook asks.

Dig to China (3:56-5:28) is the best stretch for my age group: Kansas comes out in the southern Indian Ocean, 'the people who can actually dig to China? Argentinians', the '1 IN 8' antipode map, the IF RANDOM vs REAL EARTH squares stacking into bars (4:48-4:50), and the 89% water half. These are facts you repeat to friends.

The jokes are visual and come every 30-60 s: Santa's workshop on an ice floe (3:04), the 1918 classroom 'Sleep tight, kids' (7:08-7:12), fingernails vs toenails (9:48), the Pangooy blob with its 'TUESDAY, 9:00 A.M.' calendar (12:14-12:19), the Florida moving van (13:45), 'Reminder: you're a mammal' (15:52).
The JUICE CHECK stamps work as verdict beats and as a brand device: FALSE (1:30), TRUE (9:52), IT'S COMPLICATED (14:09). The on-screen chapter titles are questions (2:56, 3:56, 5:58, 8:02, 14:36).

Loops are planted and closed: Bacon's 'is there a southern continent? Remember that' (1:15) pays off at 10:23-10:31; the Holden tease (2:41) at 12:19; Bacon's 'not... mere accident' (1:07) at 16:03 with 'It wasn't an accident. It was a breakup'; and 'the same ocean you just dug into' at 6:57.
The Wegener chapter (8:01-9:41) is the emotional peak: archival push-ins, 'Neither of them made it back', the film's only >1.2-s pause (9:39.9-9:41.1), and '1963 - 33 YEARS TOO LATE' (9:40).

The future chapter is shareable: four named supercontinents with a one-word comment prompt (15:29), the red-hot climate globe (15:48-15:52), and 'one frame of a very slow movie' over a film strip of globes (16:14-16:22), followed by a concrete next-episode tease (the Ethiopia Y-crack, 16:19-16:36).

The picture changes constantly (277 cuts; most 30-s windows have 4-20 cuts), the music changes per chapter, and the one-sentence subscribe ask (5:47-5:57) comes right after the first big payoff, over moving pictures.

(1:15) pays off at 10:23-10:32; 'Hold on to him' (2:41) at Holden, 11:34-12:38; 'pyramidal' (2:11) at Green, 6:13; 'four continents' (0:43) at 14:52-15:29; the lopsided planet (0:18) at 5:28 and 14:19; 'not an accident' (1:07) at 16:03. The Wegener death beat (9:03-9:41) uses the film's only deliberate long pauses (1.2 s after 'back.' and after 'died.') and the '1963: 33 YEARS TOO LATE' reveal. It is an emotional peak that earns goodwill for the payoff.

Transitions carry meaning: a whip down to the South Pole on 'go to the bottom' (3:10.8), a photo-negative flash on 'photographic negatives' (3:20.2), a polaroid flash on 'snapshot' (14:30.9), and the 2026-to-1620 year roll on the Bacon cards (0:55, 16:03).

The ending mechanics are right: a one-word comment prompt naming the four options (15:29), a callback, the film-strip 'one frame of a very slow movie', a concrete next-story cliffhanger (the Afar Y, 16:19), and the end screen over a still-moving map (16:35-16:51).

fatigue_points.why: The first list: seven place names in about 9 s (0:03-0:12) over a still flat map.
History chapter: four people and five dates since 0:59, mostly archival stills, then the same five names over the same map as 0:08 (2:21-2:29).
Three distances in 23 s, with the 3:09 line at about 187 wpm (2.5 mi down, about 2 mi up, 1.5 mi thick; 2:55-3:18).

This is where fatigue sets in for an average viewer: about 2 minutes at 165-195 wpm under the same 3-minute music cue, now adding one-eighth, 'less than half', 'sprinkled at random' and a mental puzzle with no time to think (4:35-5:12).
The first call to action, over a single 17-s push-in.
The rewind is shown twice (10:00-10:04, then 10:07-10:14), which feels like a repeat.
Second onset: the answer has already landed, then a blank frame and 'the honest part' signal an epilogue.
Ten proper nouns in 14 s (13:02-13:16), then Baja, Florida and Agulhas back to back.
A hedged verdict at 164-169 wpm over re-used visuals, during the lowest motion in the film (14:00-14:30).
A numbered list of four models in an identical globe template, with the 2x2 grid shown again and again.
Wrap-up signals ('Whichever future wins...', 'Four hundred years ago...') invite exits before the Ethiopia tease at 16:19.

strengths: The setup-and-payoff structure is excellent, and every thread is closed: Bacon's open question (1:15) pays off at 10:23, 'not an accident' (1:07) at 16:03, 'Hold on to him' (2:41) in the Holden twist (11:34-12:38), 'pyramidal' (2:11) at 6:13, 'Tuesday' (12:07) at 15:41, plus the 'same ocean you just dug into' callback at 6:57. Every chapter ends on the question the next one answers (2:49, 3:45, 5:39, 7:47, 9:58).
Every promise from the hook is delivered: dig to China (3:56-4:35), the 1875 theory (5:57-7:47), what the drips point at (10:14-11:34), the four crash continents (14:52-15:29).

Several set pieces genuinely win attention back: the Argentina dig (4:00-4:35), the pyramid checklist filling to a 5/5 stamp (6:28-6:47), the Gondwana assembly with its ticking counter (10:07-11:12), the scar-lines reveal (11:32), the map flip and the Blue Marble photo 'shot with Antarctica on top' (11:53-12:02), the Pangooy blob with its Tuesday calendar (12:13-12:18), and the 'slow movie' film strip (16:16-16:20).

The Wegener chapter (8:01-9:58) is the best-built stretch and should hold flattest: the letter over his eye (8:08), the 'UTTER, DAMNED ROT!' slam (8:32), the German corridor leading to the Austria door (8:35-8:39), the archival Wegener and Villumsen sequence (9:03-9:21), and '33 YEARS TOO LATE' (9:40). It also has the fewest globe shots (about 30%).

Dry, on-brand humour lands roughly once a minute: the refund (2:08), the houseboat (2:55), Argentinians (4:34), sleep tight (7:05), reckless driving (10:59), the time zone (12:07), Florida (13:27), the mammal (15:44), the breakup (16:03).
The recurring JUICE CHECK verdict stamps (FALSE 1:30, ? 5:51, TRUE 9:52, IT'S COMPLICATED 14:08) set up a payoff rhythm and build the series brand, and the music changes per chapter (10 cues).
The only real pause in the film (after 'died.' at 9:39.9) gives the emotional peak room to land, which shows what breathers would do elsewhere.

The ending follows the playbook: an honest verdict that earns trust, an easy one-word comment prompt ('Africa, Antarctica, Asia or Australia', 15:29), a 'so what' line (16:14), the Ethiopia cliffhanger (16:19), a spoken pointer to the next video plus subscribe, then a cut.

result.voice_fatigue:
Mostly fine. The cadence varies well sentence to sentence, but the overall tempo hardly changes over 17 minutes.

What works:
- Sentence shapes vary: 271 sentences, median 8 words, 22% fragments of 4 words or fewer, 13% of 16 words or more, 7% questions.
- Pauses breathe: 407 pauses of 150 ms or more (median 0.48 s). The big beats get 1.5-1.8 s holds: 552.3 'Neither of them made it back', 579.3 'after he died', 692.8 'They're scars', 630.5, 757.0, and the chapter cards at 174, 356, 480, 603 and 874.
- Pitch is expressive, not a stamped TTS cadence: the median spread within a take is 12 semitones. Sentence endings are 76% falling, 18% level and 6% rising; yes/no questions rise and wh-questions fall.
- Take loudness is steady (sd 0.25 dB), and 10 music beds change underneath.

What is flat:
- All 109 takes use the default speed (spec.json sets no 'speed'). Speaking rate stays at 3.6-4.2 syllables/s in every minute from 1 to 16, and pacing.md shows 122-178 wpm per 30 s window (106 and 62 only in the model list and the outro).
- The somber death passage starts at the same clip as the jokes: s064 is one of the fastest takes.
- 'And' opens 25 sentences and 'So' 12. A picky ear will notice, but it isn't tiring.

Two stretches carry the real fatigue risk. Both are reported as minor issues:
- 4:00-5:15 is the fastest minute, and s035 runs 27% over the median while delivering the 1-in-8 statistic.
- 12:55-14:35 is six long, uniform takes over near-still pictures, right where the answer lands.

Verdict: no fatigue problem in the first 4 minutes or in chapters 3 to 5a. Deliberate tempo changes would stop the full 17 minutes feeling like one long read: speed 0.9 on the death beat and on 'So is the drip just a coincidence?', and about 1.05 on the future-models montage.

result.verdict: No, most viewers won't reach the end, though the film is on target rather than broken. The consensus curve holds 68% at 0:30 and 58% at 1:00 (both inside the playbook's targets) and averages about 35.7% AVD (6:01 of 16:51), right at the 35% target. About 16% are still there when the voice ends at 16:38 and about 10% at 16:51. The spread by audience is wide: 28% for a Shorts-trained 19-year-old, 42% for a geography fan. Viewers tire in three places. First, 1:40-2:55, a roll-call of people who noticed the pattern (Bacon recap, Forster's flood, Humboldt, the hook's list read again, two 1970s jokes), with nothing new on the 'why' since 0:31: the curve sheds 8 points in minute 2 and 5 in minute 3, and the casual viewer leaves at 2:41. Second, and milder, 4:35-5:20: six statistics at 172-178 wpm over near-still globes under a single 3-minute music bed, which is where the average viewer starts to tire. Third, and the one that costs the ending, everything after 'They're scars' (11:33). The proof itself is a 1.3-s blur. It is followed by a tangent (Nevada), an empty frame at 12:56, the stillest minute of the film (13:30-14:30) and a 30-s recap at 14:04 that sounds like the end, so the curve sags 2.1-2.4 points a minute just before the four-continents payoff and comment prompt promised at 0:47. Between those stretches, the pyramid, Wegener and Gondwana chapters (5:57-11:12) hold at about 1.5 points a minute. Fixes 1-11 are cuts, picture-only re-renders and audio edits with no new narration. They take about 1:17 out (to roughly 15:34) and should lift AVD to roughly 39-40% and end-screen reach to about 19-20%. Order of work: apply the re-renders and the vo_proc.wav cleanup first, then make every cut in one edl.py pass. All times in this plan are on the current 16:51 master.

result.disagreements:
1) Opening motion: R2 credits the hook with 'motion from frame 1'. R1, R3 and R4 say the globe is still. Frame grabs settle it: frames 0-90 are identical and the arcs start at 0:03.3, so R1, R3 and R4 are right.
2) The history block: R1 wants a big reorder (other side and dig to China first); R3 and R4 want cuts; R2 wants a ~15-s trim. Cuts come first, because they are an S-effort edl.py pass that keeps the date order and every plant; the reorder stays optional (fix 21). They also disagree on which part to cut. R1 would drop the Bacon myth-bust (1:25.9-1:39.1) and keep Forster; R3 drops Forster. R3 is more likely right: the myth-bust carries the first JUICE CHECK stamp, while Forster plants nothing and holds five bug-finder defects. On the re-read list (2:21-2:29), R1 and R4 would cut it and R2 would keep the callback; the plan cuts the list and keeps the 'exact list you saw at the start' line.
3) SFX masking: R2 and R4 say the impact hits bury 'Eventually', 'They're scars' and 'Here's the twist'. The audio check measured the hits below 300 Hz, with the voice 15-40 dB clear at 1-4 kHz and ASR at 0.93-1.00, so the audio check is right. Only the record scratch at 9:48.5 needs moving.
4) Names: R2 would re-voice Villumsen, Amasia and Wegener. The audio check clears all but 'Wegener' at 9:50.4 (Villumsen's V/W is uncheckable and not shown on screen; Amasia is clear and labelled), and it is right. Fix that one name with a paste from 8:58.2.
5) Pacing: R4 calls the narration wall-to-wall (pacing.md lists one pause over 1.2 s). The audio check counts 407 pauses, with 1.5-1.8-s holds on the big beats, and puts the real risk only at 4:00-5:15 and 12:55-14:35. The audio check is more likely right, so the plan uses targeted holds (fix 22), not a global re-time.
6) Nevada: R3 would cut it; R4 would animate the blob. Cut it: it comes after both payoffs, it is off-question, and cutting is cheaper.
7) Florida: R3 would cut it; R1, R2 and R4 would trim and animate it. The majority is right: Florida is named in the hook and its gag lands.
8) The flipped Blue Marble aside (11:54-12:07): R1 would cut it; R4 lists it as a strength. Keep it: it is a true, surprising fact on a moving picture. Just silence the 12:03.4 fragment.
9) 'Now, the honest part, because we're not going to fake you a tidy answer': R4 would delete it as an epilogue signal; R2 counts it as a trust builder. Keep the line and fix the empty frame under it.
10) 7:36-7:42: R1 would cut it; R2 lists the pyramid deflating into a ball as a strength. Keep it and fix the still 7:16-7:24 hold instead.
11) R2 would trim the Wegener biography (8:25-8:28, 8:33.5-8:40). R1, R3 and R4 call the chapter the best-built stretch, and R4 singles out the corridor-to-Austria gag. Don't trim.
12) 9:48.6: R3 calls it a fine one-frame zoom punch; R1 says the card jerks and the whole frame stays dim. Frames show the frame darker from 9:48.73 onward, so R1 is right.
13) Subscribe: R3 says nothing on screen points to subscribing; R2 and R4 place a pill at ~5:56. Frames show the pill from 5:56.5, so R2 and R4 are right; it just needs to come in 2 s earlier.
14) 10:34.43: R1 sees one bad frame, R3 a 6-frame shake. It can't be told apart at tile resolution, and it is low severity either way.
15) R3 would add a 'JUICE CHECK: NOT A COINCIDENCE' stamp at 11:32. Declined: the on-word 'THE BIG DRIPS ARE SCARS' text already lands there, and the stamp would pre-empt the 14:09 'IT'S COMPLICATED' verdict.
16) Level and exit points: AVD ranges from 28.4% (R1) through 35.3% (R3) and 37.0% (R4) to 42.0% (R2), and the exits from 2:41 (R1) through 12:56 (R4) and 14:04 (R3) to the end (R2).
